Package org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic

Class AgenticTurnRunner

java.lang.Object
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic.AgenticTurnRunner
public final class AgenticTurnRunner extends Object
Runs one step of a turn: asks the agent what to do next and acts on what it did.

The agent is reached through the connector registry, the same way a service task with camunda:connector reaches it, so a turn uses the connector the engine has registered and configured rather than an instance of its own.

    • FOLLOW_UP_PARAMETER

      public static final String FOLLOW_UP_PARAMETER
      The connector's input parameter sent instead of the task on the first turn of a re-entry: what changed since the agent was last here, the user's feedback in a feedback loop.

      Held apart from the connector's other input parameters at parse time (AgenticAdHocParseListener.extractFollowUp), so the generic per-step evaluation in askTheAgent(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.persistence.entity.ExecutionEntity) never touches it. snapshotFollowUp(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.persistence.entity.ExecutionEntity) is the only thing that evaluates it, once, when a re-entry begins.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • FROZEN_FOLLOW_UP

      public static final String FROZEN_FOLLOW_UP
      The key snapshotFollowUp(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.persistence.entity.ExecutionEntity) freezes the result under, in the agent state's own map (CIB7-2200) -- not a variable of its own, and not of the scope execution. A value re-read from the expression would evaluate it again on every step of every turn (CIB7-2148), which could see the feedback change between this entry and whenever the first turn's job actually runs, or between two steps of that same turn. A value frozen on the scope execution would not fix that either: the scope's children are the agent's tools, they are the untrusted party, and the scope execution is their ancestor, so a tool calling execution.setVariable(FROZEN_FOLLOW_UP, ...) would overwrite it there and change what a later step of the same turn sends. The agent state execution is their sibling instead, unreachable the same way AdHocAgentState's own fields already are.

      A map entry rather than setVariableLocal(FROZEN_FOLLOW_UP, ...) directly, for the same two reasons every other field of the agent state moved into that map: a value that long -- a user's feedback, not a short token -- has no business in the engine's 4000-character string column, and a feedback loop that re-enters many times must not grow the agent state by one more variable, and one more history row at level full, per entry.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

  • Method Details

    • runTurn

      public static void runTurn(ExecutionEntity scopeExecution, CommandContext commandContext)
      Runs one step of a turn: one model call, the tools it asks for, committed together (CIB7-2148).

      A turn is as many steps as the model needs: a step whose model calls tools schedules the next one as a job of its own, and the model ends the turn by answering. A failure from here on replays one model call, not the turn, and the job lock has to cover one model call only.

    • writeAnswer

      protected static void writeAnswer(ExecutionEntity scopeExecution, Map<String,Object> response, String outcome)
      Where the answer goes: the output parameters of the agent's connector decide, as on a service task, applied after every turn -- when the model answers, not after a step in which it only called tools; without any, the answer goes to agentOutput.

      The turn's outcome goes with it (CIB7-2151): under outcome in the response, so an output parameter maps ${outcome}, and to agentOutcome when there are none. It is also kept in the step's map, for a later turn that ends the scope without writing an answer: over a cap, or after completeScope, once what still ran has ended.

      An output parameter that hands over the AI-output marker itself, whatever its expression (${outputAiMeta}, #{outputAiMeta}), stores it Java-serialized, as the agent's own variables (CIB7-2819). The marker is a map of a Boolean and Strings: under JSON with Spin's map type detector, its type would be named after the Boolean, and the variable could not be read back, nor could any read of all of the instance's variables.

    • storable

      protected static Object storable(Object value)
      A value a variable can hold (CIB7-2165). The connector hands an answer longer than a String variable's text column over as an object value, and a String that long fails the insert of the variable and of its history row. So the connector's object is unwrapped, and a String over the column becomes an object, Java-serialized like the chat log and the conversation, which every engine can write, Spin or not. Readers still get the String back. A shorter one stays a String.

    • fitsAStringVariable

      public static boolean fitsAStringVariable(String text, String databaseType)
      Whether a String variable's text column holds text: 2000 characters on Oracle, NVARCHAR2(2000), and 4000 on the others; on DB2 also no more than 4000 bytes of UTF-8, since its VARCHAR(4000) counts bytes, and text with umlauts reaches them before 4000 characters. The tool provider refuses a text argument by the same limit.

    • snapshotFollowUp

      public static void snapshotFollowUp(ExecutionEntity scopeExecution)
      Evaluates the scope's followUp expression once, for this re-entry, and freezes the result on the agent state execution -- a sibling of the scope's tools, not an ancestor, the same protection AdHocAgentState already gives its own fields (CIB7-2137).

      Called only when this entry is a re-entry (AgenticAdHocStartListener), in the same transaction the scope is entered in -- not later, when the first turn's job happens to run, and not again on a later step or turn. A scope's first entry, where the result would go unused, never calls this at all: a followUp expression that reads a variable the feedback step sets -- absent before the user has ever given feedback -- must not be able to fail a turn that was never going to use it. If evaluation fails on re-entry, a warning is logged and the task is used instead.

    • endOfTurn

      protected static void endOfTurn(ExecutionEntity scopeExecution)
      Two exits, decided by one question: is anything still running inside the scope?

      Nothing is. Then the scope ends -- either the agent asked for that, or it did not but started nothing either, and no further turn would ever be scheduled.

      Something is. Then the scope stands and that child's end brings the next turn. This holds even when the agent asked to end: ending here would cancel live work, which is the very thing completeScope refuses for, and a child can still be started from outside after the request was made. The request keeps, and the turn that child's end schedules acts on it -- see runTurn(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.persistence.entity.ExecutionEntity, org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.interceptor.CommandContext).

      Where the scope would end after a limit, and the scope asks for it with cibseven.agentic.onLimit = error, it ends with a BPMN error instead, its code the limit (CIB7-2151).

    • throwsOnLimit

      protected static boolean throwsOnLimit(ExecutionEntity scopeExecution)
      Whether a limit ends the scope with a BPMN error: cibseven.agentic.onLimit = error.

    • throwTheLimit

      protected static void throwTheLimit(ExecutionEntity scopeExecution, String limit)
      Ends the scope with a BPMN error whose code is the limit, where it would otherwise complete: the same moment, once nothing runs, so a limit still cancels no work (CIB7-2144). The parse listener has made sure a boundary event on the scope catches every limit it can reach, so the engine never ends the scope silently for want of a catch (CIB7-2151).
